Marco: hey folks — day 2 here. Quick org question: who is the owner for routing rules that decide whether traffic goes to hosted vs. dedicated? Also, if a model rollout starts failing (5xxs), who do I page/DM to kick off an emergency rollback?
Sam: welcome Marco! routing policies are primarily owned by eng-runtime. Dedicated-specific routing (tenant pins, reserved pools) is product/dedicated infra. For an immediate rollback, infra oncall executes; eng-runtime coordinates the rollback steps.
Devika: adding detail: eng-runtime handles the policy config and the rollout playbook, product owns rollout approvals for Dedicated. If it's customer-impacting, infra-sre gets paged first (sev2+), then eng-runtime oncall.
Marco: great — who specifically on eng-runtime should I add to my contacts? and is there a short runbook I can read?
Sam: ping @Omar (runtime lead) and @Devika for rollout questions. We have a tiny runbook: /docs/runbooks/rollbacks (request access via IT if you can't see it).
Omar: hi Marco  welcome! the TL;DR runbook is below. Read the "Immediate rollback" section first. DM me if you need the oncall rotation.
Omar: ```
Quick rollback steps:
1) Pager infra-sre (primary) -> tell them "model rollout 500s, request emergency rollback"
2) Infra-sre attempts remediation (config revert / scale down). If no fix -> trigger rollback artifact
3) Eng-runtime verifies traffic routing back to previous variant + sanity checks
4) Product + owning model team notified, start postmortem
If pager doesn't respond: DM Omar -> Devika -> Sam
```
Marco: perfect, thanks. I tried the doc link but got a 403. What permission group do I need?
Devika: you should be in the "redwood-staff" group. If not, open a ticket to it-requests with subject: "access docs/runbooks/rollbacks" and cc me. I'll approve ASAP.
Marco: last Q — who signs off changes that could affect latency SLOs? infra or product?
Sam: depends: infra-level infra changes need infra-sre + eng-platform signoff; runtime/model-serving config changes need eng-runtime + product signoff. High-risk changes require a signed release owner and a canary plan.
Marco: awesome, adding to my onboarding notes. thanks all! :thumbsup:
OpsBot: Reminder: Marco onboarding intro with Runtime scheduled Fri 9:30am. Link: https://meet.redwood/intro-runtime
Infra SRE: adding myself here for pager handoff help — ping me if you want the oncall cheat sheet or to shadow a pager during your first week.
